_note: Mango Code's model catalog, read by the app (engine-cfg). Adding a model = adding an entry here and its place in 'order'. The gguf/mmproj paths are relative to the models folder (mango-paths.json). 'repo', 'revision' and 'files' (path, size, sha256) say where to download a model from and how to verify it; 'ctx' and 'memory' (K+V cache per token at f16 and fixed state, from the GGUF header) estimate whether it fits in the PC's memory. How it runs on specific hardware is in profiles/.
_engine: 'requires_engine': the weights are in a format the official llama.cpp cannot read (toq): the model runs only where a profile says how. A 'files' entry with 'engine' is for that engine only: each PC downloads the files of the engine the model runs with, and that engine opens its file instead of 'gguf'.
_active_permille: In MoE models, the thousandths of the weights the engine reads for each token: the rest of the model plus the chosen experts (expert_used_count over expert_count), from the GGUF header. They tell which model is probably the fastest; in dense models it is missing (they read everything).
_ctx: 128k is Mango Code's TARGET context. A local model's 'ctx' is the maximum it supports (GGUF header): the general plan uses the smaller of the two and goes lower only if memory is not enough. A profile has the context measured on its hardware.
_order: The recommended local models in the order they are listed (selector, first run): each local model of 'models' appears once. The user's models follow, then the cloud ones.

toq._on_request: TOQ stays in the list for whoever chooses it, but it is never preselected nor marked fastest: in our tests as an agent it wrote incoherent text and ignored web search.
toq.label: Qwen3.8-27B-TOQ-v1
toq._shape: From the GGUF header, like 'memory': used to split the layers across the GPUs (engine-cfg, split.rs) to tell, before downloading, whether the model fits and with what context. At start-up the plan rereads the real header.

3.6.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
3.6._gguf: The file with the MTP head (one extra layer, +0.46 GiB): needed by the draft. The repo also has mmproj-F16.gguf, the same encoder as the file without the head.
3.6._chat_template: chat-templates/qwen3.6-mango.jinja is the GGUF's template with THREE lines added: a system message that is not the first is rendered in place instead of being silently dropped (~1600 prompt tokens would vanish), and the reasoning of past turns stays in the history (otherwise every new user message changes the previous turn and the engine re-reads all of it).

deepseek.label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
deepseek._image: The model accepts images as input. Without this line mango-code generates modalities.input=[text] and opencode rejects images (see opencode.template.json, _modalities).
deepseek._cloud: Not a local model: no gguf, no llama-server, no VRAM. The key is in the Windows Credential Manager (the app saves it from the Team settings), never here: this file is versioned. It is spoken by opencode (@ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider on OpenRouter).
deepseek._ctx: 1M, as declared by OpenRouter. The generation cap is computed as for the others (ctx/8, between 4k and 16k).

qwen.label: Qwen3.8-27B
qwen._cloud: A cloud model like deepseek, which the Team can use for its agents (-Agent qwen).
qwen._ctx: 262144 is the maximum declared by the provider that serves the model (top_provider.context_length): declaring more would make opencode compact later than the provider really accepts.

3.8.label: Qwen3.8-27B
3.8._chat_template: The GGUF template of this repo with ONE line changed: a system message that is not the first is rendered instead of raising 'System message must be at the beginning.', which would make every request with a system message in the middle answer 400. toq uses it too. It must be kept aligned if the GGUF changes.

bonsai2.label: Bonsai-2-27B
bonsai2.kind: dense 27B ternary / hybrid GDN / PrismML fork
bonsai2._files: Two variants of the same weights, one per engine ('engine' of the file): Q2_0 for the official llama.cpp (CPU, CUDA, Vulkan: every PC without a profile), PQ2_0 for the three-GPU profile's prism fork, faster. Each PC downloads only the one for its engine; the encoder is needed by both.
bonsai2._chat_template: Copy of the GGUF's template with TWO changes: a non-first system message is rendered instead of raising, and the reasoning of past turns stays in the history (see 3.6).

lfm.label: LFM2.5-24B-A2B
lfm._thinking: It always reasons (the template opens <think> at every turn) and cannot be turned off.
lfm._chat_template: Copy of the GGUF's template with ONE change: the reasoning of past turns stays in the history (see 3.6).

3.5-4b.label: Qwen3.5-4B
3.5-4b._chat_template: The GGUF's template with TWO changes: the reasoning of past turns stays in the history and a non-first system message is rendered instead of raising (see 3.6).

3.5-2b.label: Qwen3.5-2B
3.5-2b._memory: From the model's config.json: cache of 6 attention layers x 2 x 2 heads x 256 x 2 bytes = 12 KiB per token; state of 18 GDN layers x 16 heads x 128 x 128 x 4 bytes plus the convolution, about 20 MiB.
